objectives: I can say numbers 1-20 from memory.
I can listen to a short introduction and note the name, age, and country.
I can introduce myself in three sentences without looking at notes.

stages.name: Retrieval Warm-up and Bridge
stages.purpose: Same-day retrieval of numbers and key phrases from the first lesson, then bridge to production focus so pupils know what changes this slot.

procedure.text: Say: 'We practised English in our first lesson today. Let's quickly recall the numbers.' Demonstrate: say 'drei' — pupils respond 'three'.
Number call-back: teacher calls numbers 1-20 in random German order, pupils call back in English. Then reverse: teacher says English numbers, pupils count on fingers to confirm.
Quick phrase ping-pong: say a German personal question, pupils say the English version. Cover 4 phrases: Wie heisst du? / Wie alt bist du? / Woher kommst du? / Hallo!

Bridge + learning intention: 'In the first lesson you learned the words and forms. Now you use them — without the board. You will listen to new people and speak yourself.' Write on board: I can say numbers 1-20. / I can listen and note name, age, country. / I can introduce myself in 3 sentences.

stages.name: Country Words and Listening Task
stages.purpose: Pre-teach the three country names pupils need, then push Listening competence to understand depth by extracting facts from new introductions.

procedure.text: Open the country vocabulary glossary (Three Countries). Read each word together using the read-aloud button: England, Spain, Australia. Note the German cognates: England = England, Spanien = Spain, Australien = Australia.
Say: 'Draw this table in your exercise book — three columns: Name | Age | Country.' Draw it on the board.
Pupils draw the table in exercise books.
Open the reading text (Three New Classmates). Read each introduction twice at a slow, clear pace. Pause between each person.
Check answers whole-class. Ask: 'Who is first? How old is Leon? Where is he from?' Fill in the board table together. Pupils self-correct.

stages.name: Numbers Production
stages.purpose: Push Numbers competence from introduced to produce depth through a written gap-fill followed by a spoken guessing game.

procedure.text: Open the gap-fill exercise (Numbers in Sentences). Say: 'Each sentence has a number in figures. Write the number as a word. Example: 10 = ten.' Point to first item as a model.
Check answers whole-class. Write correct spellings on board: twelve (not twelfe), eleven, fifteen, twenty. Pupils correct own work.

Guess My Age: think of a number 1-20. Pupils ask 'Is it eight?' You answer 'Yes!' or 'No, higher!' / 'No, lower!' — write higher/lower on the board. Play 2 rounds, then let a pupil take the teacher role.

stages.name: Speaking Production — Partner Introductions
stages.purpose: Push Speaking competence to produce depth through pair interviews followed by third-person presentations to the class.

procedure.text: Model with one confident pupil: ask 'What is your name? How old are you? Where are you from?' Pupil answers. Then say: 'Now I introduce my partner: This is [name]. He/She is [age] years old. He/She is from [place].' Write the frame on the board.
Pairs interview each other using the three questions. Both take notes (name, age, from). After two minutes, swap roles.
4-5 pupils introduce their partner to the class using the third-person frame on the board. Class listens and checks they heard correctly.
Open the reorder exercise (Build Your Introduction) as a quick consolidation check — pupils can attempt it individually as others present.

stages.name: Wrap-up — Exit Speaking
stages.purpose: Individual spoken production check: every pupil produces at least one self-introduction sentence before leaving.

procedure.text: Say: 'Before you leave, say one sentence about yourself in English — to me, at the door.' Point to the board: I can introduce myself in 3 sentences. Aim for 3, minimum 1.
As pupils pack up and leave, each says 1-3 sentences to teacher at the door: 'My name is ___.' / 'I am ___ years old.' / 'I am from Germany.'

differentiationNotes: Weaker pupils: allow the board frame (This is ___. He/She is ___ years old. He/She is from ___.') to stay visible during partner presentations; accept a single exit sentence at the door. Stronger pupils: during the guessing game, take the teacher role and use 'higher'/'lower' themselves; during partner presentations, add a fourth sentence ('He/She has a brother/sister.' or 'He/She likes ___.').
exercisePlan: Gap-fill (Band 1 — Supported): write number words 1-20 in sentences about ages, number in figures given as hint [fk.g.numbers]
Matching (Band 2 — Guided): match person name to age and country from the listening text without re-reading [fk.k.hoer.1]
Reorder (Band 3 — Independent): unscramble self-introduction and personal question sentences [fk.k.sprechen.1, fk.g.numbers]
